name: Rust
description: Rust is a systems programming language focused on safety, speed, and concurrency without a garbage collector. It powers everything from embedded devices to cloud infrastructure.

items.title: The Rust Programming Language (The Book)

items.description: All official language docs, library specs, compiler guides, and edition notes.

items.title: The Rustonomicon

lessons.title: Getting Started with Rust
lessons.description: Install Rust, understand Cargo, create projects, write Hello World, and explore the toolchain.

lessons.title: Variables, Mutability, and Data Types
lessons.description: Variables, mutability, constants, shadowing, scalar types, compound types, and type inference.

lessons.title: Ownership and Borrowing
lessons.description: Ownership rules, move semantics, borrowing with references, mutable references, and the borrow checker.

lessons.title: Slices and References
lessons.description: String slices, array slices, string vs &str, slice patterns, and danging reference prevention.

lessons.title: Structs, Enums, and Pattern Matching
lessons.description: Struct definitions, tuple structs, unit structs, enums, Option and Result, match expressions, and if let.

lessons.title: Methods and Associated Functions
lessons.description: Method syntax, self parameters, associated functions, method chaining, and traits for shared behavior.

lessons.title: Vectors, Strings, and HashMaps
lessons.description: Vec<T> operations, String vs &str, HashMap and HashSet, iterating collections, and collection performance.

lessons.title: Error Handling: Result and Option
lessons.description: Result<T, E>, Option<T>, the ? operator, combinators (map, and_then, unwrap_or), custom error types, and error conversion.

lessons.title: Generics and Traits
lessons.description: Generic functions and structs, trait definitions, trait bounds, impl Trait, and blanket implementations.

lessons.title: Lifetimes
lessons.description: Lifetime annotations, lifetime elision rules, struct lifetimes, static lifetime, and lifetime subtyping.

lessons.title: Closures and Iterators
lessons.description: Closure types (Fn, FnMut, FnOnce), iterator adapters, iterator combinators, consuming producers, and lazy evaluation.

lessons.title: Modules, Crates, and Cargo
lessons.description: Modules and paths, module file system, external crates, Cargo.toml, features, and workspaces.

lessons.title: Smart Pointers: Box, Rc, Arc
lessons.description: Box<T> for heap allocation, Rc<T> for shared ownership, RefCell<T> for interior mutability, Arc<T> for thread safety.

lessons.title: Concurrency: Threads and Message Passing
lessons.description: Thread spawning, join handles, message passing with channels (mpsc), shared state with Arc, Send and Sync traits.

lessons.title: Async/Await and Tokio
lessons.description: Async functions, await syntax, futures, Tokio runtime, async I/O, tasks, and async patterns.

lessons.title: Unsafe Rust and FFI
lessons.description: Unsafe keyword, raw pointers, calling C functions, writing C-compatible APIs, and safety invariants.

lessons.title: Testing and Documentation
lessons.description: Unit tests, integration tests, doc tests, test organization, benchmarks, and documentation with rustdoc.

lessons.title: Macros
lessons.description: Declarative macros (macro_rules!), procedural macros, derive macros, attribute macros, and function-like macros.

lessons.title: Performance and Optimization
lessons.description: Profiling with perf/flamegraph, release optimizations, SIMD, inlining, and benchmark-driven optimization.

lessons.title: Building a CLI Application
lessons.description: Argument parsing with clap, error handling, configuration, logging, testing, and building a complete CLI tool.

lessons.title: WebAssembly with Rust
lessons.description: Compiling to WebAssembly, wasm-pack, wasm-bindgen, web-sys, DOM access, and performance considerations.
